questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my spanish language skills

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The host university had several guiding documents on their ecampus, but you had to search for them on the website. They also provided a student handbook which had a lot of helpful non-academic information about for instance housing, necessary travel documents and local transportation.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation presentation and the coordinator kept us updated through emails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was difficult since there is a lot of scam in Barcelona, so it was difficult to find something beforehand where you knew it was not a scam.
I used the student handbook provided by the host university, which had listed several rental agencies, and I was satisfied.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The uni is located in the north-west-side of the city, not centrally located. So I would recommend finding a place, which is well connected to both the uni and the rest of the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Be careful to avoid scam. For instance, you can request a videocall with the landlord.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: In the first round you had to list 10 courses, ranked by priority. Afterwards there was a change round, where you could drop or add courses, but if a course was full, you had to check reguarly if someone dropped their spot since the spot would go to the person, who then added the course first.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The coordinator sent emails on the next steps and about the proces.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In first round I was only given 28 ECTS points (all courses which I prioritised), so I needed another subject in the second round.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do the pre-registration in advance so you know which courses you can choose

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was generally lower than at UCPH, but it was different depending on the specific course

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was less reading and more focus on class participation, and learning from powerpoints and group presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Global Sales Law, Comparative Law and Conflict of Laws, Diplomatic & Consular Law and Practice, Law and Competition Policy, Comparative constitutional law, Populism as a threat to constitutionalism, democracy and the rule of law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Global Sales Law - interestering and reminded more of UCPH case-based learning

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The host institution did not advertise a lot of social activities for exchange students

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I went to the Erasmus events arranged by the Erasmus organisations. They can be found on instagram. Can recommend since you meet a lot of international students who also want to connect.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on Erasmus trips and enjoy Barcelona

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They usually eat a lot later - at 21-22

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Slow living and enjoying the city, also on normal weekdays

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be careful when finding accomodations (to avoid scam)
2. Be very careful with pickpockets (especially in metros and La Rambla)
3. Go to social events, especially at the start of the semester

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting and becoming friends with people from other countries

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding accomodation took a lot of time, but a good idea to start looking early. But also don't stress since a lot of accomodation also first become available shortly before.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
